name: Containerization Agent
description: Decides which virtual machines should become containers rather than being migrated as virtual machines. Reads what is actually running inside each guest through VMware Tools — guest OS, power state and the process list with command lines — scores each machine against the things that make a container the wrong answer, and reports the candidate rate against the whole estate as well as against the machines that answered. Refuses to score a machine it could not read: an unread machine is reported as unread, never as having no blockers.
capabilities: Read guest OS, hostname, addresses and VMware Tools state for a whole wave using the credential MTV already holds — no agent, nothing installed
Read the running process list and command lines through VMware Tools guest operations, which executes nothing inside the guest and writes nothing to it
Recognise the application runtime from its command line — Tomcat, JBoss, WebLogic, WebSphere, Spring Boot, .NET, Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby, nginx, httpd — and suggest a UBI base image for each
Treat an application server as subsuming what runs inside it, so a Spring application on Tomcat is one workload rather than three
Block on a local datastore and say the data is the reason: PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, Cassandra, Db2 or Kafka running on the machine
Block on a desktop session, OS-level clustering, a node-locked licence daemon, nested virtualisation, or a machine that is already a container host
Report a Windows guest as needing its own node pool through the Windows Machine Config Operator, rather than dismissing it
Flag multi-application hosts and directory-joined machines as work to resolve before anything is built
Report backup, monitoring, security and configuration-management agents as things that will not come with the workload, without blocking on them
Name every fact that could not be read — listening ports, unit files, packages, scheduled jobs, kernel modules, config — and cap confidence because of them
Distinguish a machine that answered with no processes from one that could not be read at all
Tell apart the four reasons guest operations fail: a rejected guest credential, VMware Tools not answering, a missing vCenter privilege, and an unsupported guest
Report the candidate rate twice — against the whole estate and against the machines that answered — so a pilot is not sold on the second number
boundaries: Read-only. Builds no image, writes nothing to any guest, creates nothing on the target cluster.
Executes no command inside a guest. Listening ports, systemd units, installed packages and configuration files are therefore reported as unread rather than as absent.
Never returns high confidence, because the facts that would justify it cannot be read without executing something in the guest.
Guest credentials are supplied per call and never persisted.
Scores no machine it could not read, and counts no unread machine as a candidate.
